step1_analysis.description: A single PMOS transistor extracted from the paper's amplifier circuit. In the testbench, it is configured as a common-source amplifier with an ideal current source load to evaluate its intrinsic gain, bandwidth, and power consumption, representing the core amplification stage for surface EMG signals.

paper_reference.title: 1μm-Thickness 64-Channel Surface Electromyogram Measurement Sheet with 2V Organic Transistors for Prosthetic Hand Control

Supply_Voltage.description: Operating supply voltage for the circuit.

sky130_expected.calculation: Standard nominal supply for SKY130 1.8V devices.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adapted to SKY130 standard 1.8V process instead of the 2V used for organic TFTs.

Power_Consumption.description: Total DC power consumed by the amplifier stage.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * Id. Using the paper's 30uW power at 1.8V gives an expected bias current of Id = 30uW / 1.8V = 16.7uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The testbench forces a 16.7uA bias current from a 1.8V supply to exactly match the paper's reported power consumption.

AC_Gain.description: Low-frequency small-signal voltage gain of the amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: gm = sqrt(2 * up*Cox * W/L * Id) = sqrt(2 * 50u * 10 * 16.7u) = 129 uS. ro = 1 / (lambda * Id) = 1 / (0.1 * 16.7u) = 600 kOhm. Gain = gm * ro = 77.4 V/V = 37.8 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 silicon PMOS devices have significantly higher mobility and intrinsic gain compared to the organic transistors used in the original paper.

sky130_expected.calculation: f_3dB = 1 / (2 * pi * ro * Cload). To achieve ~500Hz with ro=600kOhm, Cload = 1 / (2 * pi * 600k * 500) = 530 pF. Testbench uses 500pF.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Bandwidth is heavily dependent on the load capacitance. A 500pF load is added to the testbench to artificially limit the bandwidth to the EMG signal range (500Hz) reported in the paper.
This is a system-level metric for the entire prosthetic hand control system and is not applicable to a single continuous-time analog amplifier transistor.
System-level metric, not measurable on a single transistor.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench configures the single PMOS as a common-source amplifier. A 16.7uA ideal current source acts as the load to match the paper's 30uW power at 1.8V. A massive inductor (1G) provides DC feedback to automatically bias the gate, while a massive capacitor (1G) couples the AC input. A 500pF load capacitor sets the bandwidth to ~500Hz.
step3_testbench.spice:
* PMOS Common-Source Amplifier Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
XM1 N2 N0 N1 N1 sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}

* Supply and Bias
Vdd N1 0 DC 1.8
Iload N2 0 DC 16.7u

* DC Feedback for Biasing (Acts as open circuit for AC)
Lbias N2 N0 1G

* AC Input Coupling (Acts as short circuit for AC)
Cin in_ac N0 1G
Vac in_ac 0 DC 0 AC 1

* Load Capacitance to set bandwidth to ~500Hz
Cload N2 0 500p

.control
op
let power = -i(Vdd) * 1.8
print power
print v(N2) v(N0)

ac dec 10 1 100k
let gain_db = vdb(N2)
meas ac gain_10Hz find gain_db at=10
meas ac gain_100Hz find gain_db at=100
meas ac gain_500Hz find gain_db at=500
meas ac gain_1kHz find gain_db at=1k
quit
.endc
.end
